Hypnozoite dormancy durations, from a batch to each of its relapses

Source: R/metrics.R
dormancy_durations.Rd

One row per relapse (a hypnozoite_activation) whose batch's row is in the log: the days from the day its hypnozoite batch was laid down to the day it activated, latency included. An import's batch, laid down a day after its primary, counts from its own row; founder seeding lays down no batch. These are the durations of the hypnozoites that activated before the run ended, so their mean is shorter than the mean time to activation; time_to_relapse() gives the censored view, one row per batch.

Usage

dormancy_durations(events)

Arguments

events

an events table from load_events(), or a run (a vivax_run or its directory).

Value

a data.table, one row per relapse, by batch_tick, batch_pedigree_id and tick, every column an integer: human_id, batch_pedigree_id (the batch it woke from), pedigree_id (the relapse's genome), batch_tick (the day the batch was laid down), tick (the day it activated) and duration (tick - batch_tick, in days).

See also

time_to_relapse()

Examples

d <- dormancy_durations(example_run())
summary(d$duration)   # days from a batch to each of its relapses
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>    1.00   19.25   42.50   58.35   78.75  282.00
